source_text: Εἰ δὲ, ἀφελόμενος τὰ τῶν πενήτων, πένησι δίδως, κάλλιον ἦσθα μήτε ἁρπάζων, μήτε διδούς. Τί μολύνεις τὸν σαυτοῦ πλοῦτον, ἐπεισάγων αὐτῷ τὰ μὴ δίκαια κέρδη; Τί βδελυκτὴν ποιεῖς τὴν σαυτοῦ προσφορὰν ἐξ ἀδικίας, προσφέρειν ἐπιχειρῶν, ἐν ᾧ μέλλεις ἕτερον πτωχὸν ἐλεεῖν; Ἐκεῖνον ἐλέησον, ὃν ἀδικεῖς. Εἰς τοῦτον κατάχρησαι τῇ φιλανθρωπίᾳ· τούτῳ χάρισαι, καὶ πληρώσεις ἔλεον μετὰ κρίσεως. Οὐ γὰρ κοινωνήσει πλεονεξίᾳ Θεὸς, οὐδὲ λῃστῶν καὶ ἁρπάγων κοινωνὸς ὁ Κύριος· οὐδὲ ὡς ἀδύνατος τρέφειν τοὺς πένητας, ἡμῖν κατέλιπεν αὐτούς· ἀλλὰ τὴν δικαίαν καὶ φιλάνθρωπον καρποφορίαν παρ' ἡμῶν ζητῶν, εἰς ἡμετέραν εὐεργεσίαν. Ἐλεη-μοσύνη ἐξ ἀδικίας οὐ γίνεται, οὐδὲ ἐκ κατάρας εὐλογία, οὐδὲ ἐκ δακρύων εὐεργεσίαι. Λέγει ὁ Θεὸς τοῖς τὰ δάκρυα κινοῦσι τῶν ἀδικουμένων, ὅτι Ἃ ἐμίσουν, ἐποιεῖτε, ἐκαλύπτετε δάκρυσι τὸ θυσιαστήριόν μου, καὶ κλαυθμῷ καὶ στεναγμῷ. Ἐκ πόνων ἐλέησον, καὶ μὴ θέλε ἀδικεῖν, προφασιζόμενος ἐξ ἀδικίας τῷ Θεῷ προσάγειν τὸν ἔλεον. Κενοδοξία τὰ τοιαῦτα, καὶ πρὸς τοὺς ἐξ ἀνθρώπων ἐπαίνους, οὐ πρὸς τὸν ἔπαινον τὸν ἐκ Θεοῦ ἐνορῶντα. Διὰ τοῦτο καλῶς ὁ Κύριος μὴ πρὸς τὸ θεαθῆναι, φησὶν, ὑπὸ ἀνθρώπων. Ἐὰν γὰρ ὡς Θεοῦ τὴν ἐλεημοσύνην ὁρῶντος ποιῇς αὐτὴν, φυλάξῃ μὴ ποιεῖν αὐτὴν ἐκ πλεονεξίας, εἰδὼς, ὅτι τὸν ἐπόπτην Θεὸν οὐκ εὐφραίνεις. Οὕτως ἐλεημοσύνην ποιῶμεν, ἵνα ἀπολάβωμεν παρὰ Θεοῦ. Ἀποδίδωσι δὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἐκείνοις, οὓς ἐπαινεῖ· ἐπαινεῖ δὲ πλεονέκτην οὐδένα. Οὐκ ἔστι σοι δῶρα προσενεγκεῖν Θεῷ, ἐὰν λυπήσῃς τὸν ἀδελφόν. Ἐὰν προσφέρῃς, φησὶ, τὸ δῶρόν σου ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον, κἀκεῖ μνησθῇς, ὅτι ὁ ἀδελφός σου ἔχει τι κατὰ σοῦ, ὕπαγε πρῶτον, διαλλάγηθι τῷ ἀδελφῷ σῷ, καὶ τότε ἐλθὼν πρόσφερε τὸ δῶρόν σου. Μέμνησο τοῦ τελώνου Ζακχαίου, ὃς, προθέμενος ἀποδοῦναι τετραπλάσιον, εἴ τι ἐσυκοφάντησεν, οὕτω τῶν ὑπολειπομένων χρημάτων τὰ ἡμίση πτωχοῖς ἀπεμέρισεν. Ἤδει γὰρ, ὅτι Χριστὸν ὑποδέξασθαι βούλεται, καὶ οὐκ ἄλλως ἀποδέξεται Χριστὸς τὰς εἰς τοὺς πτωχοὺς φιλοτιμήσεις, εἰ μὴ λυθεῖεν αἱ κατὰ τῶν ἀδικηθέντων πλεονεξίαι. Καὶ οὕτως ὁ Κύριος ἀπεδέξατο τοῦ Ζακχαίου τὴν ὀρθότητα, καὶ ἔφη· Σήμερον σωτηρία τῷ οἴκῳ τούτῳ ἐγένετο. Καὶ ταῦτα μὲν πρὸς τοὺς ἐλεημοσύνας ποιοῦντας, ἰσότητος δὲ μὴ προνοουμένους. Πρὸς δὲ τὸν ἀδικεῖν μὲν φυλαττόμενον, ἐλεεῖν δὲ ἀμελοῦντα, λέγομεν, ὅτι Πᾶν δένδρον μὴ ποιοῦν καρπὸν ἐκκόπτεται καὶ εἰς πῦρ βάλλεται, καὶ οὐδέποτε τὸ τοιοῦτο δένδρον ἀρέσει τῷ ἐπουρανίῳ γεωργῷ τῷ λέγοντι, ὅτι Ἦλθε ζητῶν καρπὸν ἐν τῇ συκῇ, καὶ οὐχ εὗρε, καὶ κελεύοντι αὐτὴν ἐκκόπτεσθαι, ἵνα μὴ καὶ τὸν τόπον κατασχολῇ. Κατεγνωσμένος δὲ παρὰ Θεῷ φαίνεται καὶ ὁ τὸ ἐνεχύρασμα τῷ πένητι μὴ ἀποδιδοὺς, καὶ ἀπειλὴ κατὰ τοῦ τοιούτου γίνεται. Ὅτι, φησὶ, κεκράξεται πρὸς μὲ ὁ τὸ ἐνέχυρον μὴ ἀπολαβὼν, καὶ ἐπακούσομαι αὐτοῦ. Ἐλεήμων γάρ εἰμι. Δεινὸν δὲ καὶ παράνομον ἦν καὶ τὸν θερισμὸν ἐπεκθερίζειν, καὶ τὸν ἀμπελῶνα ἐπανατρυγᾷν, καὶ τὸν ἐλαιῶνα καλαμᾶσθαι, ὅτι ταῦτα πτωχοῖς ἔδει καταλείπεσθαι. Εἰ δὲ ταῦτα τοῖς ἐν νόμῳ προσετέτακτο, τί ἐροῦμεν περὶ τῶν ἐν Χριστῷ; πρὸς οὓς λέγει Κύριος· Ἐὰν μὴ περισσεύσῃ ὑμῶν ἡ δικαιοσύνη πλεῖον τῶν Γραμματέων καὶ τῶν Φαρισαίων, οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθητε εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν.
thought_title: Mercy must not be funded by injustice
orientation: Basil is addressing those who give alms but acquire their wealth by wronging the poor, and he is about to contrast this with the example of Zacchaeus and the demand for fruitfulness.
pass_a_gloss: But if, having taken away the things of the poor, you give to the poor, it would be better for you neither to rob nor to give. Why do you defile your own wealth, bringing into it unjust gains? Why do you make your own offering abominable from injustice, attempting to offer, in which you are about to show mercy to another poor person? Show mercy to that one whom you wrong. Toward this one use your kindness; to this one give freely, and you will fulfill mercy with justice. For God will not share with greed, nor is the Lord a partner of robbers and plunderers; nor as being unable to feed the poor did he leave them to us; but seeking from us the just and kind fruitfulness, for our own benefit. Almsgiving does not come from injustice, nor blessing from a curse, nor good deeds from tears. God says to those who stir up the tears of the wronged, that What I hated, you were doing, you were covering my altar with tears, and with weeping and groaning. From labors show mercy, and do not wish to do wrong, making a pretext of bringing mercy to God from injustice. Such things are vainglory, and look toward praises from men, not toward the praise from God who sees. For this reason the Lord says well, not toward being seen by men. For if you do your almsgiving as God seeing it, you will guard against doing it from greed, knowing that you do not gladden God the overseer. Thus let us do almsgiving, in order that we may receive back from God. And God gives back to those whom he praises; and he praises no greedy person. It is not possible for you to bring gifts to God, if you grieve your brother. If you offer, he says, your gift upon the altar, and there you remember that your brother has something against you, go first, be reconciled to your brother, and then coming offer your gift. Remember the tax collector Zacchaeus, who, having proposed to give back fourfold, if he had defrauded anyone, thus distributed half of the remaining money to the poor. For he knew that he wishes to receive Christ, and Christ will not otherwise accept the generosities toward the poor, unless the acts of greed against the wronged be dissolved. And thus the Lord accepted the uprightness of Zacchaeus, and said: Today salvation has come to this house. And these things are toward those who do almsgiving, but do not provide for fairness. But toward the one guarding against doing wrong, but neglecting to show mercy, we say, that Every tree not producing fruit is cut down and thrown into fire, and never will such a tree please the heavenly farmer who says, that He came seeking fruit in the fig tree, and did not find, and commanding it to be cut down, in order that it may not also occupy the ground. And condemned before God appears also the one not giving back the pledge to the poor, and a threat comes against such a one. Because, he says, the one not receiving back his pledge will cry out to me, and I will hear him. For I am merciful. And it was terrible and lawless also to glean after the harvest, and to gather the vineyard again, and to pick over the olive grove, because these things had to be left for the poor. But if these things were commanded to those under the law, what shall we say about those in Christ? to whom the Lord says: Unless your righteousness abounds more than that of the scribes and the Pharisees, you will not enter into the kingdom of heaven.

choices.why: glossary requires mercy for ἔλεος and justice for κρίσις; the phrase is the homily's central thesis
glossary mandates kindness for φιλανθρωπία, avoiding philanthropy or humanity
glossary mandates greed for πλεονεξία; here it is the unjust gain God will not share with
glossary mandates fruitfulness for καρποφορία, the good fruit God seeks
glossary mandates fairness for ἰσότης, even in dealings with slaves
glossary mandates almsgiving for ἐλεημοσύνη, concrete aid to the poor

pass_b_english: But if you take from the poor and then give to the poor, it would be better for you neither to rob nor to give. Why do you defile your own wealth by bringing unjust gains into it? Why do you make your offering abominable by trying to offer it from injustice, when you intend to show mercy to another poor person with it? Show mercy to the one you wrong. Use your kindness on him; give to him, and you will fulfill mercy with justice. For God will not share with greed, nor is the Lord a partner of thieves and robbers. He did not leave the poor to us because he is unable to feed them, but because he seeks from us a just and kind fruitfulness, for our own benefit. Almsgiving does not come from injustice, nor blessing from a curse, nor good deeds from tears. God says to those who cause the tears of the wronged: “You did what I hated; you covered my altar with tears, with weeping and groaning.” Show mercy from your labors, and do not wish to commit injustice, making injustice a pretext for bringing mercy to God. Such things are vainglory, aimed at praise from human beings, not at the praise that comes from God, toward which one looks. For this reason the Lord rightly says, “not in order to be seen by men” (Matthew 6:1). For if you practice almsgiving as though God sees it, you will guard against doing it from greed, knowing that you do not gladden God the overseer. Let us practice almsgiving in this way, so that we may receive back from God. God gives back to those whom he praises, and he praises no greedy person. You cannot bring gifts to God if you have grieved your brother. “If you are offering your gift at the altar,” he says, “and there remember that your brother has something against you, go first and be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift” (Matthew 5:23-24). Remember the tax collector Zacchaeus, who resolved to repay fourfold whatever he had defrauded, and then distributed half of his remaining goods to the poor. For he knew that he wished to receive Christ, and Christ would not accept his generosity toward the poor unless the greed against those he had wronged was dissolved. And so the Lord accepted Zacchaeus’s uprightness and said, “Today salvation has come to this house” (Luke 19:9). These words are for those who practice almsgiving but do not take thought for fairness. But to the one who guards against committing injustice yet neglects to show mercy, we say: “Every tree that does not produce fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire” (Matthew 3:10), and such a tree will never please the heavenly gardener, who says, “He came seeking fruit on the fig tree and found none,” and orders it to be cut down so that it will not use up the ground (Luke 13:6-7). The one who does not return a pledge to the poor also appears condemned before God, and a threat is made against such a person. “If the one who has not received back his pledge cries out to me,” he says, “I will hear him, for I am merciful” (Exodus 22:27). It was also a terrible and lawless thing to reap the harvest a second time, to gather the vineyard again, and to glean the olive grove, because these things had to be left for the poor. But if these things were commanded to those under the law, what shall we say about those in Christ? To them the Lord says: “Unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven” (Matthew 5:20).

problems.source_quote: Ἃ ἐμίσουν, ἐποιεῖτε, ἐκαλύπτετε δάκρυσι τὸ θυσιαστήριόν μου, καὶ κλαυθμῷ καὶ στεναγμῷ
problems.why: The quotation matches Malachi 2:13 LXX, but the source introduces it as God speaking directly ("Λέγει ὁ Θεός"), not as Malachi. The English adds a parenthetical citation that identifies the speaker as Malachi, which the source does not do here.
problems.fix: Remove '(Malachi 2:13)' or attribute to 'God says' as in the source.

problems.quote: Use your kindness fully on him
problems.why: κατάχρησαι means 'use up, expend fully, lavish'—the force is 'spend your kindness on him,' not 'use fully' in the sense of complete utilization.
problems.fix: Lavish your kindness on him; spend your kindness on him.

problems.quote: If the one who has not received back his pledge cries out to me
problems.source_quote: ὅτι, φησί, κεκράξεται πρὸς μὲ ὁ τὸ ἐνέχυρον μὴ ἀπολαβὼν
problems.why: ὁ τὸ ἐνέχυρον μὴ ἀπολαβὼν means 'the one who has not received back his pledge'—but this is the poor person from whom the pledge was taken, not someone who failed to get his own pledge back. The syntax is ambiguous but context (returning pledges to the poor) shows it's the poor creditor.
problems.fix: If the one who has not received back his pledge cries out to me
problems.ruling: Context is returning pledges to the poor; ὁ τὸ ἐνέχυρον μὴ ἀπολαβὼν is the poor person not getting his pledge back, not a creditor.

edits.old: Use your kindness fully on him

fixed: Removed the parenthetical citation '(Malachi 2:13)' because the source introduces the quotation as God speaking directly (Λέγει ὁ Θεός), not as Malachi.
Changed 'Use your kindness fully on him' to 'Lavish your kindness on him' to capture the force of κατάχρησαι ('use up, expend fully, lavish').

Left 'If the one who has not received back his pledge cries out to me' unchanged; the English accurately renders the Greek and the context makes clear it is the poor person from whom the pledge was taken.

problems.quote: If the one who has not received back his pledge cries out to me
problems.source_quote: ὅτι, φησὶ, κεκράξεται πρὸς μὲ ὁ τὸ ἐνέχυρον μὴ ἀπολαβὼν
problems.why: ὁ τὸ ἐνέχυρον μὴ ἀπολαβὼν means 'the one who has not received back the pledge,' i.e., the poor person from whom it was taken.
problems.fix: If the one who has not received back his pledge cries out to me.

problems.quote: not at the praise that comes from God who watches
problems.source_quote: οὐ πρὸς τὸν ἔπαινον τὸν ἐκ Θεοῦ ἐνορῶντα
problems.why: ἐνορῶντα modifies the one practicing almsgiving, not God; the praise comes from God who sees the deed.
problems.fix: not at the praise that comes from God, as one who sees.
problems.ruling: ἐνορῶντα is accusative, modifying the implied subject (the one doing almsgiving), not God; 'who watches' misattributes the participle.

edits.old: not at the praise that comes from God who watches
edits.new: not at the praise that comes from God, as one who sees

fixed: The first problem is not a mistranslation: the English 'If the one who has not received back his pledge cries out to me' correctly renders the source's ὁ τὸ ἐνέχυρον μὴ ἀπολαβὼν as the poor person who has not received back the pledge, so no edit is needed.

The second problem is real: ἐνορῶντα modifies the one practicing almsgiving, not God, so I changed 'from God who watches' to 'from God, as one who sees' to reflect that the practitioner sees God watching.

problems.why: καταχράομαι means 'use up, expend on,' not 'lavish'; implies directing existing resources, not abundance.
problems.fix: Use your kindness toward him; expend your kindness on him.

problems.why: ἐνορῶντα modifies 'the praise that comes from God,' not a separate person; means 'looking toward/attending to,' not 'as one who sees.'
problems.fix: not at the praise that comes from God, toward which one looks.

problems.quote: not to be seen by men
problems.source_quote: μὴ πρὸς τὸ θεαθῆναι, φησὶν, ὑπὸ ἀνθρώπων
problems.why: Missing 'the Lord says' (φησὶν) and the infinitive structure; this is a saying of Jesus, not a general principle.
problems.fix: the Lord says, 'not in order to be seen by men'

edits.old: not at the praise that comes from God, as one who sees
edits.new: not at the praise that comes from God, toward which one looks

edits.old: For this reason the Lord rightly says, “not to be seen by men” (Matthew 6:1).
edits.new: For this reason the Lord rightly says, “not in order to be seen by men” (Matthew 6:1).

fixed: Changed 'Lavish your kindness on him' to 'Use your kindness on him' because καταχράομαι means 'use up, expend on,' not 'lavish.'
Changed 'as one who sees' to 'toward which one looks' because ἐνορῶντα modifies the praise from God, meaning 'looking toward/attending to,' not a separate person.
Changed 'not to be seen by men' to 'not in order to be seen by men' to reflect the infinitive structure πρὸς τὸ θεαθῆναι, meaning purpose.

last_rejected.quote: and then come and offer your gift
last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ τότε ἐλθὼν πρόσφερε τὸ δῶρόν σου
last_rejected.why: Source has 'then coming, offer your gift'; English drops 'coming' (ἐλθών), losing the motion-to-altar.
last_rejected.fix: and then come and offer your gift
last_rejected.ruling: 'Then come and offer' captures ἐλθὼν πρόσφερε; 'come' implies motion, no meaning lost.

last_rejected.source_quote: Ὅτι, φησὶ, κεκράξεται πρὸς μὲ ὁ τὸ ἐνέχυρον μὴ ἀπολαβὼν, καὶ ἐπακούσομαι αὐτοῦ. Ἐλεήμων γάρ εἰμι.
last_rejected.why: The quotation matches Exodus 22:26-27 LXX (MT 22:25-26), but the citation should be Exodus 22:26 in Septuagint numbering, not 22:27.
last_rejected.ruling: Exodus 22:27 is a valid citation for this LXX quote; verse numbering conventions vary and this is defensible.

last_rejected.quote: making injustice a pretext for bringing mercy to God
last_rejected.source_quote: προφασιζόμενος ἐξ ἀδικίας τῷ Θεῷ προσάγειν τὸν ἔλεον
last_rejected.why: προσάγειν τὸν ἔλεον means 'to offer mercy/merciful deeds,' not 'bringing mercy to God' as if God were recipient.
last_rejected.fix: making injustice a pretext for offering merciful deeds to God
last_rejected.ruling: προσάγειν τὸν ἔλεον naturally means offering mercy to God; the rendering is within normal Greek range.

last_rejected.why: Ἐκ πόνων means 'out of/from your labors' but the context demands 'from the fruits of your labors' or 'from what you have earned'; 'from your labors' alone is unclear.
last_rejected.fix: Show mercy from what you have earned by labor
last_rejected.ruling: 'From your labors' adequately renders Ἐκ πόνων; the context clarifies the meaning without requiring expansion.
